articles.title: Attachment Styles, in Plain Language
articles.titleHinglish: Attachment Styles, Bilkul Simple Bhasha Mein
articles.content:
Two people can love each other equally and still make each other miserable, because they disagree about one small thing: what to do when there is distance between them.

One person moves closer when they feel unsure. The other needs room. Neither is wrong. But when the first person texts again and the second person goes quiet, both are convinced the other one is the problem.

That is what attachment styles describe. Not personality types, and not a horoscope — just a habit your nervous system learned early about whether closeness is safe and whether people come back.

The anxious pattern: distance registers as danger. A late reply, a flat tone, a cancelled plan, and your body reacts before your mind does. You reach out more, ask for reassurance, re-read old messages for evidence. Reassurance helps for about two hours. From outside it looks like neediness. From inside it feels like standing at a door that might not open.

The avoidant pattern: closeness registers as pressure. When someone wants more, you feel the walls come in and you need air. You go quiet, get busy, become vague about plans. From outside it looks like coldness. From inside it feels like protecting the last bit of yourself that is still yours. Often this is someone who learned early that needing people ended badly.

The secure pattern: distance is uncomfortable but not dangerous. They can say I missed you without it being an accusation, and hear I need an hour without it being a rejection. Most of this is luck of upbringing, not virtue. And it can be learned.

The cruel joke is that anxious and avoidant people find each other constantly, and each one triggers exactly what the other fears. The more one chases, the more the other retreats; the more one retreats, the more the other chases. Neither is being cruel. They are running two programs that make each other worse.

What helps is not diagnosis. It is naming the pattern out loud instead of acting it out. When I do not hear from you for a day, I start assuming something is wrong. That is mine to manage, but it helps if you tell me when you go quiet. That is different from why do you never reply, and it produces a completely different conversation.

If you lean anxious, the practice is to delay the reach — not forever, just long enough to notice that the fear passes on its own. If you lean avoidant, the practice is to say the thing before you disappear: I need a few hours, I am not leaving. One sentence prevents the panic that then produces the pressure you were escaping.

And remember the limit of all labels. Knowing your style explains where the reflex came from. It does not excuse what the reflex does to someone else. The useful question is never what am I, but what do I do with it now.
articles.contentHinglish:
Do log ek doosre se barabar pyaar kar sakte hain aur phir bhi ek doosre ko dukhi kar sakte hain, kyunki ek chhoti si baat par unki rai alag hai: jab beech mein doori aa jaaye tab karna kya hai.

Ek insaan doori mehsoos karte hi paas aata hai. Doosre ko jagah chahiye hoti hai. Koi galat nahi hai. Par jab pehla dobara text karta hai aur doosra chup ho jaata hai, dono ko lagta hai ki problem saamne wala hai.

Attachment styles yahi describe karte hain. Personality type nahi, rashifal bhi nahi — bas ek aadat jo aapke nervous system ne bachpan mein seekhi thi: kya nazdeeki surakshit hai, aur kya log wapas aate hain.

Anxious pattern: doori khatra lagti hai. Late reply, flat tone, cancel hua plan — aur aapka sharir dimaag se pehle react karta hai. Aap zyada pahunchte ho, bharosa maangte ho, purane messages dobara padhte ho saboot ke liye. Bharosa do ghante kaam karta hai. Bahar se yeh needy dikhta hai. Andar se aisa lagta hai jaise ek darwaze par khade ho jo shayad na khule.

Avoidant pattern: nazdeeki pressure lagti hai. Jab koi zyada chahta hai to deewarein paas aati mehsoos hoti hain aur hawa chahiye hoti hai. Aap chup ho jaate ho, busy ho jaate ho, plans par dhundhle. Bahar se yeh thandapan dikhta hai. Andar se apne aakhri bache hue hisse ko bachana lagta hai. Aksar yeh wo insaan hota hai jisne bachpan mein seekha ki kisi ki zaroorat padna bura khatam hota hai.

Secure pattern: doori uncomfortable hai par khatarnaak nahi. Wo "tumhari yaad aayi" bina ilzaam ke bol sakte hain, aur "mujhe ek ghanta chahiye" bina thukraye hue sun sakte hain. Ismein zyadatar parvarish ki kismat hai, koi neki nahi. Aur yeh seekha ja sakta hai.

Mazaak yeh hai ki anxious aur avoidant log baar baar ek doosre ko dhoondh lete hain, aur har ek theek wahi trigger karta hai jiska doosre ko dar hai. Jitna ek peechha karta hai, doosra utna peeche hatta hai; jitna doosra hatta hai, pehla utna peechha karta hai. Koi zulm nahi kar raha. Do programs chal rahe hain jo ek doosre ko kharab karte hain.

Madad diagnosis se nahi hoti. Madad is baat se hoti hai ki pattern ko act karne ke bajaye bol do. Jab ek din tumhara message nahi aata, mujhe lagne lagta hai kuch galat hai. Yeh sambhaalna mera kaam hai, par tum chup hone se pehle bata do to aasaan ho jaata hai. Yeh "tum kabhi reply kyun nahi karte" se alag hai, aur iska poora conversation alag hota hai.

Agar aap anxious side ho, practice yeh hai ki pahunchne mein thoda ruko — hamesha ke liye nahi, bas itna ki dikh jaaye ki dar apne aap utar jaata hai. Agar avoidant side ho, practice yeh hai ki gayab hone se pehle bol do: mujhe kuch ghante chahiye, main ja nahi raha. Ek sentence us panic ko rok deta hai jo baad mein wahi pressure banata hai jisse aap bhaag rahe the.

Aur har label ki ek limit yaad rakho. Apna style jaanna batata hai ki reflex kahan se aaya. Wo yeh maaf nahi karta ki us reflex se doosre ka kya hota hai. Kaam ka sawaal kabhi "main kya hoon" nahi hota, balki "ab main iska karta kya hoon" hota hai.

articles.title: Love Is Not a Feeling You Wait For
articles.titleHinglish: Pyaar Koi Feeling Nahi Hai Jiska Aap Intezaar Karo
articles.content:
Films taught an entire generation that love is a feeling that arrives, overwhelms you, and then continues on its own. So when the feeling gets quieter after two years, people panic. They think the love has died, when what has actually happened is that the chemical part of it has finished its job.

The early intensity is not a lie, but it is temporary by design. Novelty and uncertainty produce it, and both fade — not because anything went wrong, but because you now know this person. Nothing can stay novel while becoming familiar. That is the trade, and it is not a bad one.

What comes after is either an actual relationship, or a search for the intensity somewhere else.

This is where the useful idea sits. In the settled years, love behaves less like a feeling and more like attention. Do you know what is currently worrying them? Did you notice the haircut, the bad day, the thing they mentioned once? Did you do the boring task without making it a favour that gets mentioned later?

That sounds unromantic only if you have never been on the receiving end of it. Being consistently noticed by someone is, in practice, one of the most romantic experiences available to a human being.

There is a practical rule that comes out of this. Feelings follow behaviour at least as often as behaviour follows feelings. Wait to feel affectionate before acting affectionate, and in a stressful month you will wait a long time. Make the tea, ask the question, sit next to them instead of across the room, and the feeling frequently shows up afterwards. This is not faking. It is knowing which end of the rope to pull.

A caution, because this idea can be misused. None of this means you should manufacture warmth in a relationship that is harming you. Acting your way into affection works for a good relationship in a dry season. It does not work as a repair for contempt, or fear, or someone who does not care. Effort revives what is tired. It cannot revive what is dead, and it should never be used to talk yourself out of what you know.

The test worth applying is simple. In the quiet, ordinary weeks — no crisis, no celebration — do you feel more like yourself around them, or less? That answer is more honest than any amount of intensity, in either direction.
articles.contentHinglish:
Filmon ne ek poori peedhi ko sikha diya ki pyaar ek feeling hai jo aati hai, bhaari padti hai, aur phir apne aap chalti rehti hai. Isliye jab do saal baad wo feeling dheemi padti hai, log ghabra jaate hain. Unhe lagta hai pyaar mar gaya, jabki hua sirf itna hai ki uska chemical wala hissa apna kaam poora kar chuka hai.

Shuruaati intensity jhooth nahi hai, par wo design se hi temporary hai. Naya-pan aur anishchitta usse banate hain, aur dono khatam hote hain — isliye nahi ki kuch galat hua, balki isliye ki ab aap is insaan ko jaante ho. Koi cheez jaan-pehchaan banti hui nayi nahi reh sakti. Yeh sauda hai, aur bura sauda nahi hai.

Uske baad ya to asli rishta shuru hota hai, ya kahin aur intensity ki talaash.

Yahin kaam ki baat hai. Jamme hue saalon mein pyaar feeling se zyada dhyaan ki tarah behave karta hai. Aapko pata hai abhi unki chinta kya hai? Aapne baal katwane, kharab din, ya wo baat jo unhone ek baar boli thi — notice ki? Aapne wo boring kaam kiya bina use ehsaan banaye jo baad mein ginwaya jaaye?

Yeh sirf unhe unromantic lagta hai jinhe kabhi aisa dhyaan mila hi nahi. Kisi ka lagataar aapko notice karna, practically, insaan ke liye sabse romantic experiences mein se ek hai.

Isse ek practical rule nikalta hai. Feelings behaviour ke peeche utni hi baar aati hain jitni behaviour feelings ke peeche. Pyaar mehsoos hone ka intezaar karoge phir pyaar wala kaam karoge, to stress wale mahine mein bahut lamba intezaar hoga. Chai bana do, sawaal poochh lo, saamne ki kursi ke bajaye unke bagal mein baith jao — aur feeling aksar baad mein aa jaati hai. Yeh nautanki nahi hai. Yeh jaanna hai ki rassi ka kaunsa sira kheenchna hai.

Ek chetavani, kyunki is baat ka galat istemaal ho sakta hai. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki us rishte mein garmjoshi banao jo aapko nuksaan pahuncha raha hai. Kaam karke pyaar tak pahunchna ek achhe rishte ke sookhe mausam mein chalta hai. Yeh nafrat, dar, ya us insaan ka ilaaj nahi hai jise farq hi nahi padta. Mehnat thake hue ko zinda karti hai. Mare hue ko nahi, aur isse khud ko yeh samjhana ki jo aap jaante ho wo galat hai — yeh kabhi mat karna.

Lagane layak test simple hai. Un shaant, aam hafton mein — na koi crisis, na koi jashn — unke saath aap khud jaisa zyada mehsoos karte ho ya kam? Wo jawab kisi bhi intensity se zyada imaandaar hai, dono taraf.

articles.title: Jealousy: What It Is Actually Telling You
articles.titleHinglish: Jalan: Yeh Asal Mein Aapko Kya Bata Rahi Hai
articles.content:
Jealousy arrives with a story already attached. Within seconds of seeing something — a name on their phone, a laugh that was a little too easy — you have a full narrative, complete with betrayal and an ending. The feeling is fast, and the story feels like evidence.

It is worth slowing down enough to ask what the feeling is actually made of, because jealousy is rarely one emotion. Underneath it there is usually fear of being replaced, some old wound about not being enough, and sometimes plain information you should not ignore.

Start with the last one, because people skip it. Sometimes jealousy is accurate. You have noticed a change in how they speak about someone, or a phone that has started living face down. Dismissing every instinct as insecurity is not maturity; it is a way of gaslighting yourself. If something has genuinely changed, say so plainly and ask.

But often, jealousy is not about them at all. Notice whether the feeling arrives with a name attached — this specific person, this specific behaviour — or whether it floods in whenever your partner is happy in a room you are not in. The second one is not information about your relationship. It is information about how you feel about yourself when you are not the source of someone's happiness.

What makes jealousy dangerous is not the feeling. It is what people do with it. Checking phones, asking friends to report, testing with silence, picking a fight to force reassurance. All of it produces a short relief and a long cost, because surveillance is corrosive — even when it finds nothing, especially when it finds nothing, because then you need to check again.

The better move is to say the true sentence, which is almost always harder and shorter than the accusation. Not who is she, but: when you talk about her, I feel like I am losing my place, and I do not like feeling this way. That sentence gives the other person something they can actually respond to. An accusation only gives them something to defend.

And then do the unglamorous work underneath. Jealousy is loudest in people who have nothing much of their own going on. Not because they are weak, but because when a relationship is your only source of worth, every threat to it is a threat to everything. A life with your own work, friends, and interests does not make you immune, but it lowers the volume, because there is more than one place your value comes from.

One last thing. If your partner uses your jealousy — creating it deliberately, enjoying it, calling it proof of love — that is not romance. Someone who is glad you are afraid of losing them has told you something about themselves, and it is worth believing.
articles.contentHinglish:
Jalan apne saath ek poori kahani leke aati hai. Kuch dekha — phone par ek naam, thodi zyada aasaan hansi — aur seconds mein aapke paas poora narrative hai, dhokhe ke saath, ant ke saath. Feeling tez hai, aur kahani saboot jaisi lagti hai.

Itna dheere hona zaroori hai ki poochh sako yeh feeling bani kis cheez se hai, kyunki jalan aksar ek emotion nahi hoti. Uske neeche hota hai — replace ho jaane ka dar, kaafi na hone ka koi purana zakhm, aur kabhi kabhi wo information jise ignore nahi karna chahiye.

Aakhri se shuru karte hain, kyunki log usi ko skip karte hain. Kabhi kabhi jalan sahi hoti hai. Aapne notice kiya ki wo kisi ke baare mein kaise baat karte hain, ya phone ab ulta rakha rehta hai. Har instinct ko insecurity keh ke uda dena samajhdaari nahi hai; wo khud ko gaslight karna hai. Agar sach mein kuch badla hai, seedha bolo aur poochho.

Par aksar jalan unke baare mein hoti hi nahi. Dekho ki feeling ke saath koi naam juda hai — yeh khaas insaan, yeh khaas behaviour — ya wo har baar aati hai jab aapka partner kisi aise kamre mein khush hai jahan aap nahi ho. Doosri wali aapke rishte ki information nahi hai. Wo iski information hai ki jab aap kisi ki khushi ki wajah nahi hote to aap apne baare mein kya mehsoos karte ho.

Jalan khatarnaak feeling ki wajah se nahi hoti. Wo iski wajah se hoti hai ki log uska karte kya hain. Phone check karna, doston se report mangwana, khamoshi se test karna, jhagda karke bharosa nikalwana. In sabse thodi der ka aaram milta hai aur lambi keemat lagti hai, kyunki nigrani rishte ko gala deti hai — tab bhi jab kuch nahi milta, khaaskar tab jab kuch nahi milta, kyunki phir dobara check karna padta hai.

Behtar tareeka hai wo sacchi line bolna, jo lagbhag hamesha ilzaam se chhoti aur mushkil hoti hai. "Wo kaun hai" nahi, balki: jab tum uske baare mein baat karte ho, mujhe lagta hai meri jagah chhin rahi hai, aur mujhe yeh feel karna achha nahi lagta. Us sentence ka saamne wala sach mein jawab de sakta hai. Ilzaam sirf safai ka mauka deta hai.

Aur phir neeche ka boring kaam karo. Jalan un logon mein sabse zor se bolti hai jinke paas khud ka kuch khaas chal nahi raha. Isliye nahi ki wo kamzor hain, balki isliye ki jab rishta hi aapki poori value ka source ho, to uspar aaya har khatra sab kuch par khatra ban jaata hai. Apna kaam, apne dost, apni ruchiyaan — inse aap immune nahi ho jaate, par awaaz dheemi ho jaati hai, kyunki value ek se zyada jagah se aa rahi hoti hai.

Ek aakhri baat. Agar aapka partner aapki jalan ka istemaal karta hai — jaan bujh ke banata hai, mazaa leta hai, use pyaar ka saboot kehta hai — to wo romance nahi hai. Jise yeh achha lagta ho ki aap use khone se darte ho, usne apne baare mein aapko kuch bata diya hai, aur us par yakeen karna chahiye.
